source: Build a 3D treasure hunt where my avatar explores a storm-damaged lighthouse island, collects three signal parts, repairs the beacon, and quickly recovers after falling into the ocean.

image_prompt.text: A storm-damaged lighthouse near the centre of the island, tall enough to pull the player toward it from anywhere on the shore, with a broken beacon at its top
Hidden cutouts among the storm wreckage and rocks where a signal part can sit out of plain sight
A weathered board near the lighthouse base where the three signal parts are posted and tracked
Open ocean surrounding the island on all sides, with a shoreline the avatar can fall off

layout_placement.text: Three signal parts placed around the island as objective pickups
An objective board tracking which of the three signal parts are still missing
Recovery points along the shoreline so a player who falls into the ocean is returned to solid ground quickly instead of restarting
A repair interaction at the beacon that resolves once all three signal parts are carried back

notes: Scavenger Hunt preset taken whole; alcove-secret and tracker-quest were not asked for by the prompt.
No loaded option covers the beacon repair objective or the surrounding water body; both carried as id:null.
checkpoint-respawn is being used for 'quickly recovers after falling into the ocean', which is a soft recovery rather than a save point.

open_questions.ask: Should the island read as weathered photoreal coastal, or bright and stylized with cartoon storm damage?
Is this a small island you can cross in under a minute, or a larger one worth several minutes of walking?

coverage_missing.ask: Should the island read as weathered photoreal coastal, or bright and stylized?
How big is the island — a short walk around, or a few minutes to circle?
Does repairing the beacon end the game, or does it open something further?

answers.ask: Should the island read as weathered photoreal coastal, or bright and stylized with cartoon storm damage?
answers.answer: Use a weathered photoreal coastal look, with visible storm damage around the lighthouse and shoreline.

answers.ask: Is this a small island you can cross in under a minute, or a larger one worth several minutes of walking?
answers.answer: Make it a small island that can be crossed in under a minute, keeping the treasure hunt compact and playable.
